tree_reuse_decision.reason: Seventeen of the twenty existing nuclear-tree tips already have conservative source-backed binary orientation states, with both states well represented (9 vs 8).

interpretation: Unlike the current colour state panel (17 coloured / 3 white), the same 20-tip nuclear panel has a nearly balanced source-backed orientation contrast. Once the full Comp1061 occupancy/paralog gate yields an accepted branch-length tree, orientation can move directly to a preflight transition-count, ER/ARD model-adequacy and ancestral-state sensitivity analysis without waiting for two additional fixed-white nuclear lineages.
claim_boundary: The 17 resolved orientation states are taxon-concept annotations, not phenotypes measured on the exact primary sequencing vouchers. Missing/conflicting/nonbinary taxa remain unresolved. The crosswalk supports reuse of the planned branch-length tree and a preflight evolutionary analysis only; it does not establish the number of independent transitions, ancestral head orientation, parallel/convergent evolution, selection, or focal causal fitness effects. Population-aware or same-voucher validation remains required before a final repeated-evolution claim.
